newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sustainability, criteria important for EMU-EU envoy.
newsitem.headline: Sustainability, criteria important for EMU-EU envoy.

text.p: The European Union's ambassador to Japan said on Tuesday that both entry criteria and sustainability should be carefully considered by countries thinking of joining Europe's single currency.

"Both criteria and sustainability will be important considerations for political decisions of which countries group to the euro," Joern Keck, the European Union's ambassador to Japan, told a news conference in Tokyo after speaking at the Global 24 international forex conference.

Yoh Kurosawa, Industrial Bank of Japan's chairman of the board of directors, told the same news conference that the appropriate dollar/yen rate after the launch of the euro would be 110 to 120 yen to the dollar.
He added that he expects the dollar to eventually settle at around 110 yen.
The dollar was trading at about 115 yen in late Asian trade on Tuesday.
He also said a possible global shift in foreign reserves from dollars to the euro is already factored into financial markets and that the shift is not expected to cause confusion in the markets.
